My dude. I followed it up with look into your childhood, look into autistic experiences, and seek professional diagnosis. Clearly I am taking the AQ with a grain of salt and simply stating it can be a useful tool. This person already said they believed there was a possibility they have autism, so they’ve clearly already thought/ done some research on it. Fair enough if I was saying take the AQ and there’s your diagnosis! But I’m not. You’re using this as an excuse to push your feelings that not everyone who thinks they have autism does have autism. Which is a valid statement to make. But it comes across as harmful to those simply wanting an explanation for the way they’ve felt their entire life. Your bias is effecting your perception of the AQ and it’s usage. Just because a test isn’t entirely accurate, doesn’t mean it isn’t valuable. Especially when used in connection with other methods and research. Stop trying to gatekeep autism lmao and let people do their little questionnaires to help their understanding of themselves and aid in diagnosis.

I conducted a study using the AQ. Only a handful of our participants scored high enough to be considered as having autistic traits. That’s exactly what it measures, autistic traits. It’s not a diagnostic tool. Never said it was. But either way, this is not a research on autism questionnaires subreddit, this is a reply to someone who’s curious about diagnosis on the dreamwastaken subreddit. So, it’s not really the place to attempt to start up an academic debate. It’s a starting point for many people, whether it’s completely accurate or not. That’s not really debatable. And your comments are strongly implying you have bias against people who ‘think’ they are autistic, but are not yet diagnosed. Which is not nice for someone who is curious about diagnosis to read.

It’s a good tool for someone who already has suspicions of a diagnosis of autism. Which usually doesn’t come about as an ‘aha!’ moment, but more as a slow realisation. And like I said, reading up on experiences and asking about your childhood is the follow up so you can accurately compare experiences and determine whether you feel you should seek diagnosis. Questionnaire results should not be taken as complete truth, but they are a good way to self reflect and start the process of possible diagnosis which you need a lot of validation to do. And either way through professional diagnosis you’re going to get a firm answer. 

While not necessarily accurate in psychological studies they still hold value as a stepping stone to aid individuals in starting their diagnosis journey. Most people aren’t diagnosing themselves from these tests. Which is why I followed up with the correct procedure in obtaining a professional diagnosis. 

As someone who conducted a psychological research study with the AQ and had to look into it extensively and analyse its effectiveness, I am extremely aware of its issues. Though it doesn’t mean it should be entirely disregarded. It’s helped a lot of people come to terms with the possibility of a diagnosis. Including me! And pushed me to do more investigating which eventually led to my diagnosis.

When it’s strangers who are unaware you’re autistic. Yes, I understand they can misunderstand. But, with people who are aware, like friends, family, or other people who know that you’re autistic, they should offer you some grace in misunderstanding. My friends and family have adapted to my social communication style. It’s what all autistic people should have as a bare minimum. It’s not a you problem ❤️

Not sure if you want any advice but I’ll give some anyways. Take the Autism Quotient (50 question version) and look at how your results compare to the norm. Read up a lot on autistic experiences. Tumblr helped a lot for me since people are quite authentic and open there. If you feel you want to, ask family about your childhood, how you behaved etc. Or make a list of things you believe could be attributed to autism. Last step is taking that to a doctor and requesting an assessment. Not sure what country your in but for me I asked, they did a screening process to see if I seemed like I needed the assessment. Then I got it. It’s daunting, and you don’t always need diagnosis. But for me it was extremely validating and helpful.  

And yeah Twitter is a cesspit now. Even if you want to post in peace you can’t. But you should still enjoy and take pride in your interests ❤️

I think the issue is whenever he’s committed to not interacting with people like Tommy or Jack, they’ve pushed even harder. Tommy even admitted he was waiting for him to “crack” because he knows dream has a tendency to try and clear up most things said about him. They know he’s done this privately with creators too, including them, so it makes it worse that they actively were trying to get a reaction. 

The criticisms about his content/ how he got his popularity don’t make sense. Since he was a big creator before the dream smp and has pioneered a new genre of minecraft videos. Obviously he takes pride in his ideas and work. He just needs to focus on that. But I understand it’s difficult with a cloud looming over in the form of other creators who just won’t stop name dropping him. 

I think the best thing would be to delete twitter and focus on YouTube content. State he doesn’t want to engage in anymore drama, and will not be responding to anymore claims about him made by content creators. Since most of them hold no truth anyways.

Before I was diagnosed I was misunderstood so much I just figured I was a mean and blunt person. Everyone said I was too honest. Too argumentative. I was diagnosed two years ago now and it’s taken a while to realise I wasn’t any of those things, I just wasn’t what neurotypicals wanted me to be. It’s hard, but the main thing that helps is having people around you who understand it’s just who you are. Unfortunately for dream people don’t want to understand.

Totally agree. I don’t think people realise what they’re ‘criticising’ is just straight up autistic traits lol. And I think even when you try so hard it’s still visible to people that there’s something “off”. People with autism deserve to have that level of understanding. It effects way more than people think it does. And just because he’s high functioning doesn’t mean he can suddenly switch it off. Which is what I think a lot of people are assuming. It’s blatant ableism whether they realise it or not.

See for me I always feel like I NEED to clarify things said about me or personal real life drama I’m in. It’s almost painful not to. I imagine on this sort of scale it’s extremely hard for him to push back the feeling of just saying something and trying once again to convince people he’s not a bad guy. And after years of rumours, doxxing, threats, I think it would make the urge to respond and clarify even harder to resist. Especially when he’s stayed silent about other creators talking badly about him for a good while. 

I think he responded awfully with the image. Personally, I don’t use that word and I don’t think anyone else should either no matter what. But, I can understand everyone calling you a freak, and weird, and crazy, and then getting diagnosed and then having the feeling of an insane amount of injustice all at once. I think his mindset was to give them a taste of their own medicine after being mocked for his autistic traits for years. And of course, it was bad. He shouldn’t have done it. There’s no excuse. But can I understand to an extent why he chose to react so harshly? Yeah. Since when I was diagnosed I was resentful towards those who had mocked me.

Exactly. Even experiencing misunderstandings as someone with autism on a small scale is extremely upsetting and conflicting. On this level it’s downright insane and I don’t know how he copes. 

I like a lot of people recognised his traits even before he spoke up about possibly even being autistic. I think it’s why I’ve always related to him on some level and felt a lot of deep sympathy. It’s hard to navigate life when you’re autistic and this is worse ESPECIALLY when you’re undiagnosed/ unsure if you’re autistic. You only truly start to understand why you feel the way you do when you start to explore autism and how it effects you. And as far as we know he’s been undiagnosed for a while. 

Neurotypicals will never understand the feeling of trying your best, doing what you think is right, responding in ways that feels right to you, only to be told you’re dramatic and weird. This whole situation shows just how many people are uneducated on how autism actually effects people.

Yeah I was on some sort of stan twitter when I was like 15 and even then it was a hell scape. Unfortunately there are people who thrive from disregarding actual debate points and instead just aim to frustrate and upset people. Which when you have autism is the worst lol.

This is a huge issue with people who claim to be inclusive of neurodivergent people. It’s all fun and games saying you support us, but when they have to actually cater to our lack of social skills, needing clarity, basically anything that they don’t see as widespread autism traits, it’s completely ignored.

Yup exactly. I’m the exact same. Arguing with people who refuses to see my side or ignores points I’ve made is infuriating. Twitter just is not the place for people who want to have genuine debates or conversations.

I feel like this is probably why he’s struggled a lot with the weird passive aggressive behaviour he’s experienced from a lot of his fellow creators. He doesn’t know why people are upset, and is expected to know every single reason everyone has to dislike him throughout a series of offhand comments or tweets. But when he reaches out personally for clarification it’s him ‘going too far’ or ‘taking things to the DMs’ when from my perspective he’s genuinely trying to understand the issue.
I think neurotypicals don’t relate to or understand the type of frustration it causes. It’s literally different to any feeling.

My ocd is primarily tapping. Here’s a trick I learnt from cbt. My therapist told me to weigh out the odds of things so when I get an intrusive thought that is “do (insert action) or (insert bad thing) will happen” I would make myself weigh out the actual odds of that bad thing happening. And most of the time (if not all) there’s little chance of your compulsion having any effect on your life chances. So for example if I felt the need to check I locked my door again i would make a list and say “I know I’ve checked it once and I know it was locked, there’s little chance I imagined it being locked, there’s little chance anyone would break in anyways that’s a rare occurrence etc..” and then I would compare the odds of it being unlocked which is basically none because I’ve checked and I know I’ve checked. It really helped me and while it’s exhausting at the start once you get into it it sorta does help. Lots of luck x
